changes: Kālidāsa: roles changed from commissioner+owner to author (compiler). 'saṃcaya yāṅā' and 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ' mean he compiled the work. They are not commissioning or ownership formulas. Confidence lowered to medium.
Evidence extended to include 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ'.
Notes expanded: the compilation date may coincide with this copy, the final line is corrupt, and the era is assumed.

persons.name: Kālidāsa
persons.evidence: śrīkālidāsena saṃcaya yāṅā | umeśāprītaye tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ

purpose: for the pleasure of Bhavānīśaṅkara (Umeśa); merit (puṇyayoga)
notes: The era is not named. NS is assumed because the script is Newari and the colophon is in Newari (NS 752 ≈ 1632 CE). The text says Kālidāsa compiled (saṃcaya yāṅā / saṃcita) the tantra in NS 752 ('thvadaṃ' = 'this year'). This may record when the compilation was made, so the manuscript could be his own or an autograph copy. However, the colophon does not explicitly call him the scribe or commissioner. The catalogue gives Pūrṇānaṃdanātha as scribe, but that name does not appear in this colophon; perhaps it comes from elsewhere in the manuscript. The final pāda 'tayor anter ayo ʼstute' is corrupt; perhaps 'tayor antar ... astu te'. Bhavānīśaṅkara and Umeśa are deities and are not counted as persons.
